notes: Parser-resilience sanity-check for muse: a single bash tool call (python3 -c "print('x'*200000)") drives a large tool_result_batch_committed line. muse is a single-birth FilesUnderRoot+JSONLineParser adapter (agent.go), so it runs over the SAME shared core/pkg/tailer (readLineCapped, maxTranscriptLineSize=64MB, issue #270): below the cap a line parses normally; at/above it the line is logged-and-skipped past, never truncated into a partial record and never wedging subsequent lines. turn_start/turn_end are pinned same_session_as:session_birth because muse spawns goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents on every prompt that skip the ready birth and go straight to working (format-spec §9) — an unpinned matcher can vacuously bind to a subagent's own arc instead of the parent's, exactly as the sibling 2-2_auto-executed-tool-call cell's live recording exposed and fixed. No teardown/process_exited phase is asserted, mirroring 2-13_turn-end-terminal-text's precedent, because the OPEN #1962 processlifecycle race can misattribute process_exited to a reminder-subagent's late PID re-registration. RECORD-TIME CORRECTIONS (two, both live-confirmed): (1) the assessment's claim that 'muse does not itself cap or summarize tool stdout before writing it to session.jsonl' is FALSE for large outputs — the live recording's tool_result_batch_committed record carries original_output_bytes:200001, output (the actual persisted text) truncated to 99,758 bytes, and an explicit truncated:true flag. muse's OWN agent runtime truncates large tool stdout around ~100,000 bytes before it ever reaches the transcript; parser.go's parseToolResultBatchCommitted has no truncation logic of its own (still true), but that is no longer the operative ceiling — muse's own truncation is far below the 64MB tailer cap, which makes a tool-result-driven line ever reaching that cap organically much harder than assessed (a single command's output no longer scales the line size past ~100KB; the largest line this recording produced was 123,810 bytes, and that one came from an UNRELATED model_request_configured/run_context_messages record, not the recipe's own tool call). This does not change daemon_capability (below-cap lines still parse normally either way; genuine >64MB behavior is still pinned agent-agnostically by core/pkg/tailer/large_line_test.go, not by any live CLI recording) but corrects the 'large tool result is the real candidate' reasoning: for muse specifically, the tailer's cap is not the binding constraint in practice — muse's own truncation is. (2) The FIRST live attempt with an under-specified prompt ('...and then tell me only the exact character count of its output') did not even reach muse's truncation ceiling: the model piped the command through wc/od/a subprocess wrapper and reported a 196-byte summary instead of the raw blob, so the recipe's send text was tightened to explicitly forbid wc/od/summarizing and require verbatim raw stdout before this (successful) re-recording. VACUOUS-PASS CAVEAT (unchanged, now resolved): the recipe's bash command is a single unchained invocation (no && or for); this recording confirms no waiting/approval detour occurred (no state_transition to waiting anywhere in the recording).
